doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Getting a first record deal with Orrin Keepnews at Fantasy
summary: After the Columbia demo was rejected, Soskin went to Orrin Keepnews and was hired on the spot; the record came out on Prestige. He still records for SteepleChase.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh I have. You know I mean besides Sonny Rollins I played with well Stanley Turrentine, Billy Cobham, you know a bunch of people. And I saw that on one of your shows you had Orrin Keepnews, right? And Orrin was my first producer on my first record. Okay? So one thing led to another. I mean first what happened was that I was scheduled to play with the CBS All Stars, a group called the CBS All Stars and they were all all-stars and I wasn’t. So I went up to Bruce Lundvall, then the head of Columbia Records. I said, “Hey Bruce, they’re all all-stars and I’m not, so what are we going to do?” And right there he said, “Well why don’t you go in and do a demo. Put down the money.” And I did a demo and it got rejected from Columbia but I went to Orrin Keepnews and I got hired on the spot and that was it. That was the start of my career.
The record came out on Prestige and that was, you know, a little subsidiary of Fantasy you know.
Right. Well he certainly, Orrin must have recognized something in you that he liked right away and also he might have sensed there’s some longevity here.

Yes. But it was only one record. I was scheduled to do another record but, and I had all the musicians, I had, you know the compositions. But that never happened for some reason or another. But look I’m still recording. I’ve done four CDs for SteepleChase, here’s one of them. This is my last record. It’s called “Ballad for a Rainy Afternoon.” And I’m still working on, I still compose like crazy. I do a lot of composing.
